description: Source-bound Human Capability Atlas with complete deterministic artifact receipts, implementation fingerprinting, normalized exact/semantic inventory, repository snapshot, public-intake preflight, transactional intake/batch/finalization markers, sealed resumable production and full evidence-chain verification.
why_it_matters: Makes machine capability growth understandable, teachable, searchable, and ready for interface matching without replacing technical source declarations.
examples: Batch-ingest a directory of mixed capability registries while preserving rejects and provenance.
Classify duplicate IDs as exact duplicates, revisions, or conflicts without auto-merging them.
Search human-readable capabilities locally with visible ranking reasons.
Compare two registry snapshots and identify which cards, courses, graphs, and interface recommendations require re-evaluation.
typical_goals: Convert existing machine declarations into source-linked human capability knowledge
Keep a large capability registry understandable, searchable, teachable, and incrementally maintainable
Identify which downstream interfaces and learning materials require rechecking after capability changes
required_machine_actions: Detect source format
Extract candidate records
Preserve source pointers and hashes
Validate normalized sources
Generate Capability Cards and explanation views
Classify duplicate and revision groups
Build relationship and learning graphs
Audit human usability
Build deterministic search indexes
Verify review-ledger hash chains
Snapshot registries and calculate change impact
Verify strict inference evidence and source hashes
Write producer receipts after completed card builds
Reuse only receipt-verified unchanged outputs during resumed intake
Produce a no-merge-claim intake gate report
Seal raw source trees before long intake
Create deterministic non-overlapping record batches
Verify moved batch outputs against plan and producer receipts
Refuse final completion when planned coverage has gaps, extras, source drift, or unsealed scope
Join declared capability providers and consumers to registry/modules.json
Follow referenced module manifests and contracts without guessing paths
Keep module-wide context separate from capability-specific facts
Rebuild affected cards when enrichment evidence changes
Reconstruct generated public discovery outputs from the supplied tools-index snapshot
Separate provider-backed capability targets from consumer-only dependency references
Preserve public proof ceilings without claiming runtime proof or human approval
Generate deterministic context-only humanization seeds
Bind plans and receipts to the exact installed Module One source/schema fingerprint
Bind every accepted normalized source before planning
Regenerate and compare deterministic human/learning artifacts during receipt verification
Invalidate old completion evidence before replacement work
Retain in-progress markers on failed transactions
Re-verify the complete source-to-production evidence chain

required_inputs: One JSON/JSONL capability file or a directory containing manifests
optional_inputs: Human names, teaching metadata, test evidence, relationship metadata
input_constraints: Records need a stable explicit ID or an ID-keyed registry position; ambiguous list records are rejected

expected_outputs: Source-linked normalized records and Capability Cards
Quick, Practical, and Deep human views
Identity, lifecycle, duplicate, graph, coverage, and search reports
Read-only update impact and rebuild plans
output_constraints: Original source files are not rewritten
Duplicates and aliases are not silently merged
Change plans do not delete or mutate local files
Search and coverage scores expose their deterministic reasons and formulas
Shared-contract compatibility is exact and never inferred from matching major versions
Duplicate JSON object keys are rejected as ambiguous source data
A valid-looking output without a matching producer receipt is not proof of a completed Atlas run
COMPLETE_VERIFIED is plan/source-chain completeness, not Merge Gate acceptance
Batch work must follow the deterministic plan rather than worker-selected ranges
Final production remains held when upstream source scope is unsealed or unresolved

failure_modes: A broad generic alias could map a legacy field to the wrong meaning
A previously unseen manifest structure may remain unrecognized
A stable ID may be reused without a revision update
Incomplete relationship declarations may make graph impact incomplete
A named review-ledger actor may not be cryptographically authenticated
A source file can become unavailable after a receipt was produced, making strict provenance unverifiable until the exact bytes are restored

known_limitations: The complete real current AXM registry has not been ingested under v0.11 in this environment
Module Two and Module Three have not been executed against this v0.11 package here
Implementation SHA-256 fingerprints provide integrity evidence but are not cryptographic publisher signatures
Exact Python/jsonschema runtime versions are not included in the implementation fingerprint
Evidence-chain completion is not runtime capability proof

recommended_learning_steps: Preserve the v0.5.0 package and stable handoff anchor unchanged
Install v0.6.0 and run the 56-test suite locally
Run ingest against a copy of the real capability registry
If interrupted, rerun with --resume rather than restarting from zero
Review intake_gate_report.json, rejects, identity groups, graph integrity, and producer receipt failures
Compare the exact Module Two shared schema and stable anchor
Run paired round-trip fixtures through both modules
Merge only through Merge Gate after local verification
advanced_operations: Add a source-specific adapter with fixtures
Resolve duplicate and alias conflicts through review
Compare registry snapshots after GitHub pushes
Route affected capability cards into Human Interface Intelligence
common_mistakes: Treating inferred human labels as source facts
Treating a canonical selection proposal as an automatic merge decision
Treating a high coverage score as permission to ignore blockers
Applying a registry diff plan as file deletion without review
